title: perf(duct): reuse one ssh master per grove via ControlMaster + ControlPersist
description:
## .what

reuse one ssh connection per remote grove for the duct pollers (OpenSSH `ControlMaster` / `ControlPersist` / `ControlPath`), instead of a full ssh handshake per poll.

## .why

- the duct pollers check remote state with repeated short ssh calls, e.g. `ssh -n -o ConnectTimeout=8 <grove> tmux has-session -t <name>`
- measured on a dev box: a 10s churn sample saw **~100-140 distinct short-lived `ssh` processes**; each one pays a tcp connect, key exchange, and auth
- `ssh_config(5)`:
  - `ControlMaster` lets ssh listen for and share a master connection
  - `ControlPersist` keeps the master open in the background after the first client closes — indefinitely, or until idle for a set time
  - `ControlPath` names the control socket; the man page recommends at least `%h`, `%p`, `%r` (or `%C`) in a directory not writable by others

## .proposed shape

- the duct ssh calls (or the grove host entries they use) set `ControlMaster auto`, a per-host `ControlPath` such as `~/.ssh/cm-%C`, and a bounded `ControlPersist` (e.g. `10m`) so an idle grove releases its master
- the poller's per-call `ConnectTimeout` stays, so a dead master falls back loud, never hangs

## .acceptance

- consecutive polls of one grove reuse one master connection (`ssh -O check <grove>` reports a live master)
- measured before/after: distinct `ssh` processes and handshakes per 10s sample

## .sources

- https://man.openbsd.org/ssh_config
